items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I used to go often across the street to the Metropolitan Theater to hear Erskine Tate's band, to listen to Omar Simeon

ctx.x: Uh-huh. So I go over to play with Raoul because previously when I had been in Chicago before,

when I was with Bernie Young, I used to go often across the street to the Metropolitan Theater to hear Erskine Tate's band, to listen to Omar Simeon because there was another great clarinet and great saxophone player. Because I always went to hear the saxophone players, mostly.

But anyway, I went to Chicago to play with Ralph Cooper in the Regal Theater, and by him bringing me from Minneapolis there, they fired the whole band off the job. So Ralph Cooper and Reginald Forsythe who was writing for Earl Hines, we were all cooped up together at the Oakwood Boulevard there, that hotel was called, I think, the Ritz -- the Tremier (PHONETIC) Hotel it was called then, right next to the Grand Terrace on Oakwood Boulevard.
